description: Run a comprehensive GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) readiness analysis on a domain. Checks robots.txt, llms.txt (note: llms.txt is not currently supported by major AI models - having one cannot hurt but is not a meaningful optimization), homepage HTML (16 scoring categories), sitemap.xml, and security headers. Returns an overall weighted score (0-100) with per-category breakdowns and actionable recommendations. Before analysing, decide what kind of page this is (look at it or call extract_page_content, which returns the detected type and the text) and pass page_type; without it, checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. Here the page is the site's homepage: pass "homepage" unless the front page is itself another kind of page (a news front or blog index is "index", a one-page local business site is "service", a single-product site is "product"). The response includes a 'Trust Signal Evidence' section (htmlLang, hreflangs, nav/footer link anchor text + href). IMPORTANT: the Entity & Authority heuristic for about/contact/legal/imprint/cookies uses a pattern fallback. When the site is not in English (htmlLang != 'en' or hreflangs indicate otherwise), you (the calling LLM) should inspect navLinks/footerLinks semantically and override the heuristic classification in your final explanation - the anchor text tells you what each link is regardless of URL patterns. When recommending fixes, never advise renaming or 301-redirecting existing, established URLs to make slugs more descriptive or to match navigation labels: Glippy does not score slug/nav alignment, and slug readability is a minor signal meant for new pages. Only recommend a redirect for URLs that are actually broken (for example a path agents keep requesting that returns 404). Use output_format='json' to get the full raw result (includes homepage.analysis.evidence) for programmatic use.

domain.description: The domain to analyse, e.g. "example.com". Do not include https:// prefix.

max_pages.description: Maximum pages to crawl (1 = homepage only, up to 10 for multi-page analysis). Defaults to 10.

output_format.description: Output format. "text" (default) returns a human-readable report. "json" returns the raw analysis result object that can be passed to export_report's analysis_result parameter.

page_type.description: What kind of page it is, as you judged it. One of: homepage (The front page of a site or brand: what it offers and where to go next); product (One product for sale, with its price, options and details); category (A shop listing of several products, often with filters and sorting); article (A news story, blog post, guide or essay); index (A news front, blog index or hub page that lists and links to other pages); docs (Technical documentation, a reference page or a dictionary entry); faq (Questions and answers, or a help-centre article about a product or service); service (A business selling a service: trades, practices, restaurants, agencies or software); lodging (A hotel, B&B, campsite or holiday rental with rooms to book); event (One event, concert or show with its date, venue and tickets); recipe (A recipe with ingredients and steps); info (Information from a government body or a nonprofit organisation); contact (Contact details, an about page, terms, privacy or an imprint); forum (A discussion thread, or a question with answers from users). Without it (or with "auto"), checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. An unknown value is ignored with a note. One id applies to the homepage, the page this report details. A map of URL -> id also sets crawled pages it names, e.g. {"https://example.com/": "homepage", "https://example.com/blog/launch": "article"}; other crawled pages run unconfirmed.

render_mode.description: How to fetch HTML. "static" (fast, plain Node fetch) is default for this tool. "auto" tries static first and falls back to a local headless Chrome for bot-blocked responses (401/403/407/429/503 or empty 2xx). "chrome" always renders via Chrome. Chrome modes need a local Chrome binary (CHROME_PATH) or an attached instance (CHROME_REMOTE_URL).

name: analyze_domain
